title.en: Hot holding: the trace, the band, the two-hour limit

goal.en: Hot holding keeps cooked food at 60 to 85 degC. The envelope check reads the probe trace; the limits pack says what counts as time out of temperature control and what the device does about it.

note.en: A pot held at 75, 68 and 63 degC over an hour: inside the band.
The same pot falling to 55 degC: left the envelope.
The default pack: below 60 degC for more than two hours the food is discarded or reheated; the device alerts.

expect.limits[7].source: WHO Five Keys to Safer Food

note.en: The vocabulary names the hazard: time and temperature.
With a core probe the hold is verified by the probe; the ladder falls back to estimate and time for devices without one.

cli: printf '[{"t": 0, "tempC": 75}, {"t": 30, "tempC": 68}, {"t": 60, "tempC": 63}]' > trace.json && cookwala envelope cw.op.hold trace.json
printf '[{"t": 0, "tempC": 75}, {"t": 30, "tempC": 62}, {"t": 60, "tempC": 55}]' > trace.json && cookwala envelope cw.op.hold trace.json

outcome.en: You can audit a holding log with the same four words a device uses and point to the limit and its source. The humanitarian profile (scenarios 060 onwards) applies the same rule to distributions.
